note: He passes the exclusion — boxing, jiu-jitsu and marathon running are not the profile of someone gym-averse — but misses everywhere else that could be tested. A salaried Safety and Training Specialist at a water utility is not the business owner or physician the ICP describes. The ask is explicitly rescue rather than good-to-great: 'I do need to lose weight... I've been trying to lose weight for years now. I just, not very good at it.' And health is not the neglected corner of an otherwise sorted life; it is an active and repeatedly failed project interrupted by knee injuries. The income criterion is deliberately omitted from both arrays rather than guessed: it was never tested, because no coaching price was ever quoted and no financial question was asked. That omission is itself the finding — the rep disqualified this prospect on impression before the one criterion the ICP is most often decided on had been examined at all.
